topic: Binary search on a sorted array
prompt: Given a sorted array that may contain duplicates and a target, return the index of the first occurrence of target, or -1 if it is absent.
signal: Sorted input and a position query; O(log n) is expected.
key_idea: lo=0, hi=n; while lo<hi: mid=(lo+hi)/2; if a[mid] < t: lo=mid+1 else hi=mid. Return lo if lo<n and a[lo]==t else -1.

prompt: Packages with positive weights w[i] (w non-empty) must be shipped in the given order within D >= 1 days. Each day the ship carries a contiguous run of packages whose total weight is at most its capacity. Return the minimum capacity that ships everything in D days.
signal: Minimize a value where feasibility is monotonic: if capacity c works, every c' > c works too.
key_idea: lo=max(w), hi=sum(w). feasible(c): days=1, load=0; for x in w: if load+x > c: days++, load=0; load+=x; return days<=D. While lo<hi: mid=(lo+hi)/2; if feasible(mid): hi=mid else lo=mid+1. Return lo.

topic: Binary search on rotated array / peak
prompt: A sorted array of distinct integers was rotated at an unknown pivot (e.g. [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]). Return the index of target in O(log n), or -1.
technique: Modified binary search on a rotated array
signal: Sorted-but-rotated input with an O(log n) requirement.
key_idea: lo=0, hi=n-1. While lo<=hi: mid=(lo+hi)/2; if a[mid]==t return mid. If a[lo] <= a[mid] (left half sorted): if a[lo] <= t < a[mid] then hi=mid-1 else lo=mid+1. Else (right half sorted): if a[mid] < t <= a[hi] then lo=mid+1 else hi=mid-1. Return -1.

topic: Binary search on rotated array / peak
prompt: Given an array where nums[i] != nums[i+1] and nums[-1] = nums[n] = -infinity, return the index of any element strictly greater than its neighbors, in O(log n).
signal: O(log n) on an unsorted array; a local property tells you which side must contain an answer.
key_idea: lo=0, hi=n-1; while lo<hi: mid=(lo+hi)/2; if a[mid] < a[mid+1]: lo=mid+1 (a peak exists on the rising side) else hi=mid. Return lo.

prompt: Given an array sorted in non-decreasing order and a target, return the 1-based indices [i, j] (i < j) of the two numbers that add up to target, using O(1) extra space. Exactly one solution exists.
signal: Sorted array, pair search, constant space.
key_idea: l=0, r=n-1. While l<r: s=a[l]+a[r]; if s==t return [l+1, r+1]; if s<t: l++ else r--.

prompt: Given heights h[i] of vertical lines, find two lines that together with the x-axis hold the most water. Return that area.
signal: Pair maximization where moving the shorter side is the only move that can improve the result.
key_idea: l=0, r=n-1, best=0. While l<r: best=max(best, min(h[l],h[r])*(r-l)); if h[l] < h[r]: l++ else r-- (move the pointer at the shorter line). Return best.

prompt: Return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
technique: Variable-size sliding window (last-seen index map, or a set while shrinking left)
signal: Longest contiguous substring satisfying a constraint that you can restore by shrinking from the left.
key_idea: last[c]=-1 for every character c; l=0, best=0. For r in 0..n-1: if last[s[r]] >= l: l = last[s[r]]+1; last[s[r]]=r; best=max(best, r-l+1). Return best.

prompt: Given strings s and t (t non-empty), return the shortest substring of s that contains every character of t (with multiplicity). If several shortest windows exist, return the leftmost; if none exists, return an empty string.
signal: Minimum contiguous window covering a multiset.
key_idea: need=count(t), missing=len(t), l=0, bestL=0, bestLen=inf. For r in 0..|s|-1: if need[s[r]] > 0: missing--; need[s[r]]--. While missing==0: if r-l+1 < bestLen: bestL=l, bestLen=r-l+1; need[s[l]]++; if need[s[l]] > 0: missing++; l++. Return "" if bestLen==inf, else s[bestL : bestL+bestLen].

prompt: Given an integer array (values may be negative) and k, count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k.
signal: Subarray sum target with negative values, which rules out a sliding window. sum(i..j) = P[j] - P[i-1].
key_idea: cnt={0:1}, p=0, ans=0. For x: p+=x; ans+=cnt[p-k]; cnt[p]++. Return ans.

prompt: Given a fixed m x n matrix, answer up to 10^5 queries for the sum of the submatrix (r1,c1)-(r2,c2).
signal: Many range-sum queries over a static grid.
complexity: O(mn) build, O(1) per query, O(mn) space

prompt: Start from an array of n zeros. Apply up to 10^5 updates of the form (l, r, v) with 0 <= l <= r < n, meaning add v to every index in [l, r]. Return the final array.
signal: Many range updates, read once at the end.
key_idea: d = n+1 zeros. For each update: d[l]+=v; d[r+1]-=v. Then s=0; for i in 0..n-1: s+=d[i]; out[i]=s. Return out.

prompt: Group a list of lowercase strings into groups of anagrams. Groups and the words inside them may be returned in any order.
signal: Group items by an equivalence that has a canonical form.
complexity: O(n * k log k) time with a sorted key, or O(n * k) with a 26-count key; O(n * k) space (k = max word length)
key_idea: groups = empty map. For each word: key = sorted(word), or its 26-count tuple; groups[key].append(word). Return the values of groups.

prompt: Given an unsorted integer array, return the length of the longest run of consecutive values (e.g. [100,4,200,1,3,2] -> 4), in O(n).
signal: An O(n) requirement rules out sorting; you need membership checks.
key_idea: s=set(nums), best=0. For x in s: if x-1 not in s: y=x; while y in s: y++; best=max(best, y-x). Return best (0 for empty input).

prompt: Return the maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
signal: Best contiguous subarray in one pass.
key_idea: cur = best = a[0]. For x in a[1:]: cur = max(x, cur + x); best = max(best, cur). Return best. (Starting best at 0 breaks on all-negative input.)

prompt: Sort an array containing only 0s, 1s and 2s in place, in a single pass.
signal: Three distinct keys, one pass, in place.
key_idea: lo=mid=0, hi=n-1. While mid<=hi: 0 -> swap(lo,mid), lo++, mid++; 1 -> mid++; 2 -> swap(mid,hi), hi-- (do not advance mid).

prompt: An array of n integers has every value in [1, n]. Some values appear twice and others are missing. Return all missing values in increasing order, in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
signal: Values lie in [1, n], so each value maps to an index; O(1) space means using the array itself.
complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space (output not counted)
key_idea: Index marking: for each x in a: i=|x|-1; a[i] = -|a[i]|. Then for i in 0..n-1: a[i] > 0 means i+1 is missing. Cyclic sort alternative: for i in 0..n-1: while a[i] != i+1 and a[a[i]-1] != a[i]: swap a[i] with a[a[i]-1]. Then for i in 0..n-1: a[i] != i+1 means i+1 is missing.

prompt: Given an unsorted integer array, return the smallest missing positive integer in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
signal: The answer is in [1, n+1]; place each value v at index v-1.
key_idea: For i in 0..n-1: while 1<=a[i]<=n and a[a[i]-1] != a[i]: swap a[i] with a[a[i]-1]. Then the first i in 0..n-1 with a[i] != i+1 gives i+1; otherwise the answer is n+1.

prompt: Given a list of closed intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return them sorted by start. Intervals that touch (e.g. [1,4] and [4,5]) overlap.
signal: Overlapping ranges must be combined.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
key_idea: Sort by start. out=[]. For cur in sorted order: if out is non-empty and cur.start <= out.last.end: out.last.end = max(out.last.end, cur.end); else append cur. Return out.

prompt: Given meeting time intervals [start, end) with start < end, return the minimum number of conference rooms required. A meeting ending at time t and one starting at t can share a room.
technique: Sweep line (or a min-heap of end times)
signal: Maximum number of overlapping intervals at any point.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
key_idea: Events (start,+1) and (end,-1), sorted by time with ends before starts at equal times; cur=0, best=0; for each event: cur+=delta, best=max(best, cur). Return best. Alternative: sort by start; empty min-heap of ends; for each meeting: if heap is non-empty and heap.top <= start: pop; push end. Return the heap size.

prompt: Given an array of up to 10^5 integers, count the pairs (i, j) with i < j and a[i] > a[j].
technique: Merge sort with counting (or a Fenwick tree / BIT)
signal: Pairwise order count where n is too large for O(n^2).
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
key_idea: sortCount(a): if n<=1 return (a, 0). Recursively sortCount the left and right halves. Merge with i=j=0, cnt=leftCnt+rightCnt: if left[i] <= right[j]: take left[i], i++; else take right[j], j++, cnt += len(left)-i. Append leftovers. Return (merged, cnt). Use a 64-bit counter (up to ~5*10^9 pairs).

prompt: Find the k-th largest element (1 <= k <= n, counting duplicates, i.e. the element at index n-k in sorted order) of an unsorted array in average O(n) time.
signal: A single order statistic is needed, not a full sort.
complexity: O(n) average, O(n^2) worst time; O(1) extra space iterative (O(log n) average recursion). Heap alternative: O(n log k) time, O(k) space
key_idea: target=n-k, lo=0, hi=n-1. Loop: v = a[random index in lo..hi]; 3-way partition a[lo..hi] into <v | ==v | >v (lt=lo, i=lo, gt=hi; while i<=gt: if a[i]<v swap(a[lt],a[i]), lt++, i++; elif a[i]>v swap(a[i],a[gt]), gt--; else i++). If lt <= target <= gt return v; if target < lt: hi=lt-1 else lo=gt+1.

prompt: Given an array and k (1 <= k <= number of distinct values), return the k most frequent elements, in any order, in O(n) time. The answer is guaranteed to be unique.
signal: Frequencies are bounded by n, so you can index buckets by count.
key_idea: cnt = frequency map. buckets = n+1 empty lists; for (x, f) in cnt: buckets[f].append(x). out=[]. For f from n down to 1: for x in buckets[f]: append x to out; if len(out)==k return out.

prompt: Given non-negative integers, arrange them to form the largest number and return it as a string (e.g. [3,30,34,5,9] -> "9534330").
signal: The order depends on the pairwise concatenation result, not on numeric value.
key_idea: Convert to strings. Sort so that a comes before b if a+b > b+a, then join. If the result starts with '0', return "0".

prompt: Given daily temperatures, return for each day the number of days until a warmer temperature (0 if none).
signal: Next greater element for every index.
key_idea: ans = n zeros; stack of indices, initially empty. For i in 0..n-1: while the stack is not empty and t[i] > t[top]: j = pop, ans[j] = i - j. Then push i. Return ans.

prompt: Given non-negative bar heights of a histogram (width 1 each), return the area of the largest rectangle (0 if there are no bars).
signal: For each bar you need the nearest smaller bar on both sides.
key_idea: Append a sentinel 0 to h; stack of indices, initially empty; best = 0. For i in 0..len(h)-1: while the stack is not empty and h[i] < h[top]: height = h[pop]; width = i if the stack is now empty, else i - top - 1 (top after the pop); best = max(best, height*width). Then push i. Return best.

prompt: Given an array of n numbers and a window size k (1 <= k <= n), return the maximum of every contiguous window of size k, left to right.
signal: Max or min over a sliding window, in O(n).
key_idea: Deque of indices, initially empty, values decreasing front to back. For i in 0..n-1: while the deque is not empty and a[back] <= a[i], pop the back; push i at the back; if front <= i-k, pop the front; if i >= k-1, emit a[front].

prompt: Decode a valid string like "3[a2[c]]" -> "accaccacc", where k[s] means s repeated k times (k is a positive integer, possibly multi-digit; s is lowercase letters and nested groups). Brackets can nest.
signal: Nested brackets whose inner result feeds the outer one.
complexity: O(n + d*L) time (L = output length, d = max nesting depth; O(n + L) when nesting is shallow), O(n + L) space
key_idea: cur = empty string builder, num = 0, stack empty. Digit: num = num*10 + digit. '[': push (cur, num), then cur = new empty builder, num = 0. ']': pop (prev, k); append cur's contents to prev k times; cur = prev. Letter: append it to cur. Return cur's contents. (Plain string concatenation cur = prev + cur*k recopies prev at every ']' and can cost O(L^2).)

prompt: Evaluate a valid string expression with non-negative integers, '+', '-', parentheses and spaces (e.g. "1 - (2 + 3) + 4"). '-' may also be unary at the start or right after '(' (e.g. "-(2 + 3)", "1 - (-2)").
signal: Expression evaluation with nesting.
key_idea: res = 0, sign = 1, num = 0, stack empty. Space: skip. Digit: num = num*10 + digit. '+' or '-': res += sign*num, num = 0, sign = +1 or -1. '(': push res, push sign, then res = 0, sign = 1. ')': res += sign*num, num = 0, then res = pop_res + pop_sign*res. At the end return res + sign*num.

prompt: Reverse the nodes of a linked list k at a time (k >= 1). If fewer than k nodes remain at the end, leave them as is. Relink nodes (do not change values) and use O(1) extra space.
signal: Re-link segments without extra memory.
key_idea: dummy.next = head, groupPrev = dummy. Loop: kth = groupPrev moved k steps forward; if it becomes null, stop. nextGroup = kth.next, oldHead = groupPrev.next. Reverse the group: prev = nextGroup, cur = oldHead; while cur != nextGroup: nxt = cur.next, cur.next = prev, prev = cur, cur = nxt. Then groupPrev.next = kth and groupPrev = oldHead (oldHead.next already points to nextGroup). Return dummy.next.

prompt: Given a linked list, return the node where a cycle begins, or null if there is no cycle. Use O(1) space.
signal: Cycle detection with constant space.
key_idea: slow = fast = head. While fast and fast.next: slow = slow.next, fast = fast.next.next; if slow == fast, break. If the loop ended without meeting, return null. Then slow = head; while slow != fast: slow = slow.next, fast = fast.next. Return slow.

prompt: Determine whether a singly linked list is a palindrome using O(1) extra space.
technique: Fast/slow pointers to find the middle, then reverse the second half
signal: Compare both halves without random access or extra memory.
key_idea: slow = fast = head; while fast and fast.next: slow = slow.next, fast = fast.next.next. Reverse the list starting at slow (prev = null); q = its new head, p = head. While q: if p.val != q.val, the answer is false; p = p.next, q = q.next. Otherwise true. (Optionally reverse the second half back before returning.)

prompt: Sort a linked list in O(n log n) time.
technique: Merge sort on a linked list: split at middle + merge two sorted lists (or bottom-up merge sort for O(1) space)
signal: Linked lists have no random access, so merge sort fits naturally.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(log n) recursion stack (O(1) bottom-up)
key_idea: sort(head): if head or head.next is null, return head. Split at the FIRST middle: slow = head, fast = head.next; while fast and fast.next: slow = slow.next, fast = fast.next.next; right = slow.next; slow.next = null. l = sort(head), r = sort(right). Merge: tail = dummy; while l and r: take the node with the smaller val (l on ties), append it, advance; append the leftover list; return dummy.next.

prompt: Given n points (n much larger than k, 1 <= k <= n), return the k points closest to the origin (Euclidean distance), in any order. If several points tie at the k-th distance, any of them may be returned.
signal: Top-k of a large stream or array.
complexity: Heap: O(n log k) time, O(k) space. Quickselect: O(n) average (O(n^2) worst) time, O(1) extra space.
key_idea: d(p) = x*x + y*y (no sqrt needed). Heap: for each point push (d(p), p) into a max-heap; if its size exceeds k, pop the max. Return the heap's points. Quickselect: partition the array around a random pivot by d until the pivot lands at index k-1 (recurse into the side containing k-1); return the first k points.

prompt: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
technique: K-way merge with a min-heap (or divide-and-conquer pairwise merging)
signal: Several sorted sources; repeatedly take the global minimum.
complexity: O(N log k) time (both approaches), O(k) heap space
key_idea: Min-heap of (val, idx, node) ordered by val, then idx. Push each non-null head. tail = dummy. While the heap is not empty: pop (v, i, node); tail.next = node, tail = node; if node.next exists, push (node.next.val, i, node.next). Return dummy.next. Alternative: merge lists in pairs, halving the count each round.

prompt: Design a data structure with addNum(x) and findMedian() over a stream of numbers. findMedian is called only after at least one addNum; with an even count it returns the mean of the two middle values.
technique: Two heaps (max-heap for the low half, min-heap for the high half)
signal: A running median, or the middle of a dynamic set.
complexity: O(log n) add, O(1) median, O(n) space
key_idea: low = max-heap, high = min-heap. addNum(x): push x into low; pop low's top and push it into high; if size(high) > size(low), pop high's top and push it into low. findMedian: if the sizes are equal, (low.top + high.top) / 2, else low.top.

prompt: Return the maximum path sum in a non-empty binary tree, where a path is a sequence of at least one node connected by edges, each node used at most once, and can start and end at any node (values can be negative).
technique: Postorder DFS returning the best single-branch gain
signal: Combine child results at each node; the answer may bend through a node.
key_idea: best = -infinity. gain(null) = 0. gain(n): gl = gain(n.left), gr = gain(n.right); best = max(best, n.val + max(0,gl) + max(0,gr)); return n.val + max(0, gl, gr). Call gain(root), return best.

prompt: Return the k-th smallest value (1-indexed, 1 <= k <= number of nodes) in a binary search tree.
signal: Inorder traversal of a BST yields sorted order; stop early.
key_idea: Stack empty, cur = root. While cur or the stack is not empty: while cur: push cur, cur = cur.left. cur = pop; k -= 1; if k == 0, return cur.val; cur = cur.right.

prompt: Return the values visible from the right side of a binary tree, top to bottom.
signal: Per-level information (the last node of each level).
key_idea: If root is null, return []. Queue = [root]. While the queue is not empty: n = len(queue); for i in 0..n-1: pop the front; if i == n-1, record its val; enqueue its non-null left, then right. DFS alternative: dfs(node, depth) visiting right before left, recording node.val when depth == len(result).

prompt: Determine whether a binary tree is a valid binary search tree: every value in a node's left subtree is strictly less than the node's value and every value in its right subtree is strictly greater (so duplicate values make it invalid). An empty tree is valid.
technique: DFS with (low, high) bounds (or an inorder strictly-increasing check)
signal: The BST property is global, so checking only parent vs child is not enough.
key_idea: valid(n, lo, hi), where lo/hi = null means no bound: n is null -> true; if lo != null and n.val <= lo -> false; if hi != null and n.val >= hi -> false; return valid(n.left, lo, n.val) and valid(n.right, n.val, hi). Call valid(root, null, null) (not INT_MIN/INT_MAX, which break on those values).

prompt: Given a binary tree (not a BST) and two nodes p and q in it, return their lowest common ancestor.
signal: Find the deepest node whose subtree contains both targets.
key_idea: If node is null, p or q, return node. l=lca(left), r=lca(right). If both are non-null, return node; otherwise return whichever is non-null.

prompt: Design functions that serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize the string back into the same tree.
technique: Preorder DFS with null markers (or BFS level order with null markers)
signal: Encode structure plus values so it can be rebuilt unambiguously.
key_idea: ser: preorder; emit str(val) for a node and '#' for null, joined by ','. deser: split on ','; i = 0; build(): tok = tokens[i], i += 1; if tok == '#', return null; node = new node(int(tok)); node.left = build(); node.right = build(); return node. Return build().

prompt: Given a 2D grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), count the islands (4-directionally connected land).
signal: Connected components on a grid.
key_idea: Scan every cell. When a cell is '1': count++, then flood fill from it (DFS/BFS over 4-directional '1' neighbors), setting each reached cell to '0' so it is never counted again. Return count.

prompt: Given beginWord, endWord (beginWord != endWord, all words the same length) and a word list, return the number of words in the shortest sequence from beginWord to endWord where adjacent words differ in exactly one letter and every word after beginWord, including endWord, is in the list. Return 0 if no such sequence exists.
signal: Shortest path with unweighted edges.
complexity: O(N * L^2 * 26) time, O(N * L) space
key_idea: Put the list in a set. Queue = [(beginWord, 1)]. Pop (w, d); if w == endWord, return d. For every position and every letter a-z, build the candidate; if it is in the set, remove it from the set and enqueue (candidate, d+1). If the queue empties, return 0.

prompt: In a grid, 2 = rotten, 1 = fresh, 0 = empty. Each minute, rotten oranges rot their 4-directional fresh neighbors. Return the minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if that is impossible.
signal: Several sources spread simultaneously; you need the distance to the nearest source.
key_idea: Enqueue all rotten cells and count the fresh ones; minutes = 0. While the queue is non-empty and fresh > 0: minutes++, then pop exactly the cells that were in the queue at the start of this round, and for each fresh 4-directional neighbor set it to rotten, fresh--, and enqueue it. Return minutes if fresh == 0, else -1 (no fresh oranges at the start returns 0).

prompt: Given numCourses (courses 0..numCourses-1, numCourses >= 1) and prerequisite pairs [a, b] (take b before a), return any order that takes every course exactly once and respects all pairs, or an empty list if impossible.
technique: Topological sort (Kahn's BFS, or DFS reverse postorder)
signal: Ordering under dependencies, with cycle detection.
key_idea: Add an edge b -> a for each pair and compute indegrees. Enqueue every node with indegree 0. Pop a node, append it to the order, decrement each out-neighbor's indegree, and enqueue those that reach 0. If len(order) < V there is a cycle: return []; else return order.

prompt: A graph started as a tree on n nodes, then one extra edge was added. Given the edges in order, return the edge that can be removed so the graph is a tree again (the last such edge in the input).
signal: Edges arrive incrementally; detect the first edge that joins already-connected nodes.
key_idea: For (u,v): if find(u)==find(v), return [u,v]; otherwise union(u,v). Use path compression and union by rank or size.

prompt: In a directed graph on nodes 1..n with non-negative edge weights (travel times), a signal is sent from node k. Return the time for all nodes to receive it, or -1 if some node never does.
signal: Single-source shortest paths with non-negative weights.
complexity: O(E log V) time, O(V + E) space
key_idea: dist[k] = 0, all others inf. Min-heap of (dist, node) starting with (0, k). Pop (d, u); skip if d > dist[u]; for each edge u->v with weight w, if d+w < dist[v], set dist[v] = d+w and push (dist[v], v). The answer is the max dist over all nodes, or -1 if any is still inf.

prompt: Given n cities, flights (u, v, price) with price >= 0, src and dst, find the cheapest price from src to dst using at most k stops (at most k+1 flights), or -1 if no such route exists.
technique: Bellman-Ford limited to k+1 rounds (or level-limited BFS, or Dijkstra over (node, stops))
signal: Shortest path with a bound on the number of edges.
key_idea: dist[v] = inf for all v, where inf + w must not overflow (e.g. inf = 1e9 in 64-bit ints); dist[src] = 0. Repeat k+1 times: tmp = copy(dist); for each (u,v,w): tmp[v] = min(tmp[v], dist[u]+w); dist = tmp. Return dist[dst], or -1 if dist[dst] >= inf. Copying is what enforces the edge limit.

prompt: There are n <= 100 cities (0..n-1) with weighted bidirectional roads (positive weights; a pair may have several roads). For each city, count the other cities whose shortest-path distance from it is <= distanceThreshold. Return the city with the smallest count; on a tie, return the largest index.
signal: All-pairs distances on a small n.
key_idea: d[i][j] = inf (inf + inf must not overflow), d[i][i] = 0, and for each road (u,v,w): d[u][v] = d[v][u] = min(d[u][v], w). for k: for i: for j: d[i][j] = min(d[i][j], d[i][k]+d[k][j]). For each i, count j != i with d[i][j] <= threshold. Scan i in ascending order and take i whenever count <= best count, so ties go to the larger index.

prompt: In an m x n grid each cell has an arrow: 1 right, 2 left, 3 down, 4 up (it may point outside the grid). Moving to the neighbor the arrow points to costs 0; changing a cell's arrow (at most once per cell) costs 1. Return the minimum total cost to make a path from the top-left to the bottom-right.
signal: Shortest path where every edge weight is 0 or 1.
key_idea: dist = inf everywhere, dist[top-left] = 0, deque = [top-left]. Pop u from the front; for each in-grid 4-directional neighbor v: w = 0 if u's arrow points to v, else 1; if dist[u]+w < dist[v], set dist[v] = dist[u]+w and push v to the front if w == 0, else to the back. Return dist[bottom-right].

prompt: Given n >= 1 points, the cost to connect two points is their Manhattan distance. Return the minimum cost to connect all points.
technique: MST (Prim's on a dense graph, or Kruskal's)
signal: Connect everything at minimum total edge weight.
complexity: Prim O(n^2) for a dense complete graph; Kruskal O(n^2 log n)
key_idea: Prim: best[v] = inf for all v, best[0] = 0. Repeat n times: pick the unvisited v with the smallest best[v], mark it visited, add best[v] to the total, and set best[u] = min(best[u], dist(v,u)) for every unvisited u. Kruskal: sort all n(n-1)/2 edges by weight; for each (a,b,w), if find(a) != find(b), union them and add w.

prompt: Given a directed graph as an adjacency list, determine whether it contains a cycle. Explain how the method differs for an undirected graph.
technique: DFS with three colors (or Kahn's: cycle if fewer than V nodes come out); parent tracking or DSU (undirected)
signal: Detect a back edge.
key_idea: color: 0=unvisited, 1=on the current path, 2=done. For each node with color 0, DFS(u): color[u]=1; for each neighbor v: if color[v]==1, cycle; if color[v]==0, DFS(v); then color[u]=2. Undirected: DFS(u, parent), where a visited neighbor that is not the parent means a cycle; or DSU: for each edge, find(u)==find(v) means a cycle, else union(u,v).

prompt: Given n people (1..n) and pairs who dislike each other, can you split everyone into two groups so that no disliking pair is in the same group?
signal: Two groups with conflict edges across them.
key_idea: For each uncolored node, color it 0 and BFS. For each neighbor of a popped node: if uncolored, give it 1-color and enqueue it; if it has the same color, return false. Return true after all nodes are colored.

prompt: Given an undirected connected network of n servers with no repeated connections, return every connection whose removal would disconnect some servers.
signal: Critical edges, i.e. bridges.
key_idea: DFS from node 0 assigning disc[u]=low[u]=time++. For each neighbor v other than the parent (safe because connections are never repeated): if unvisited, recurse, set low[u]=min(low[u],low[v]), and if low[v] > disc[u] then (u,v) is a bridge; otherwise low[u]=min(low[u],disc[v]).

prompt: Given distinct positive candidates and a target, return all unique combinations that sum to target. Each candidate can be used unlimited times.
signal: Enumerate all combinations under a constraint.
complexity: Exponential, roughly O(n^(T/min)) time; O(T/min) recursion depth
key_idea: dfs(start, remain): if remain==0, record a copy of path and return. For i from start to n-1: if c[i] <= remain, push it, call dfs(i, remain-c[i]) (i, not i+1, allows reuse), then pop. Start with dfs(0, target).

prompt: Given an array that may contain duplicates, return all unique permutations.
technique: Backtracking with a used[] array and duplicate skipping
signal: Permutations with duplicates require pruning identical branches.
complexity: O(n * n!) time, O(n) extra space
key_idea: Sort first. dfs: if len(path)==n, record a copy and return. For each i: skip if used[i], or if i>0 and a[i]==a[i-1] and not used[i-1]. Otherwise used[i]=true, push a[i], recurse, pop, used[i]=false.

prompt: Return the number of ways to place n queens on an n x n board so that no two attack each other.
technique: Row-by-row backtracking with column and diagonal sets
signal: Place items under constraints; prune invalid partial states.
key_idea: dfs(r): if r==n, count++. For c: if c, r-c and r+c are all free, add them to the sets, call dfs(r+1), then remove them.

prompt: Given a grid of letters and a non-empty word, return whether the word can be spelled by moving between 4-directionally adjacent cells, using each cell at most once.
signal: Path search where cells cannot be reused.
key_idea: Return true if dfs(r,c,0) holds for any cell. dfs(r,c,i): return false if (r,c) is out of bounds or grid[r][c] != w[i]; if i is the last index, return true. Mark the cell by overwriting it with a sentinel (so the char check also rejects visited cells), try the 4 neighbors with i+1, restore the cell, and return whether any succeeded.

prompt: Given intervals [start, end], return the minimum number of intervals to remove so that the rest do not overlap. Intervals that only touch, like [1,2] and [2,3], do not overlap.
signal: Maximize the number of non-overlapping intervals.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(1) extra space beyond the sort
key_idea: Sort by end. lastEnd = -inf, kept = 0. For each interval: if start >= lastEnd, keep it (kept++, lastEnd = end); otherwise remove it. Answer = n - kept.

prompt: Given nums where nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i, determine whether you can reach the last index starting from index 0.
technique: Greedy farthest reach (or backward greedy: track the leftmost index known to reach the end)
signal: Reachability where only the farthest reachable index matters.
key_idea: far=0. For i: if i > far, return false; far = max(far, i+nums[i]). Return true.

prompt: On a circular route, station i has gas[i], and driving to station i+1 costs cost[i]. Return the starting index that completes the circuit, or -1. The answer is unique if it exists.
signal: If you run dry at j starting from s, no station in [s, j] can be the start.
key_idea: If sum(gas) < sum(cost), return -1. Otherwise tank=0, start=0; for i: tank += gas[i]-cost[i]; if tank < 0: start=i+1, tank=0. Return start.

prompt: Design a structure with addWord(w) and search(w) over lowercase words, where a search pattern may contain at most 2 '.' characters, each matching any single letter.
signal: Prefix-based storage with character-by-character matching.
complexity: O(L) add; search O(L) without wildcards, worst case O(26^2 * L) under the 2-dot limit
key_idea: Each node has children[26] and an end flag. addWord walks the letters, creating missing children, and sets end on the last node. search(node, i): if i == len(w), return node.end. If w[i] == '.', return true if search(child, i+1) holds for any non-null child, else false. Otherwise go to the child for w[i]; return false if it is null.

prompt: Given a letter grid and a list of up to 3*10^4 words, return every word that can be spelled on the grid (adjacent cells, no cell reused within a word).
signal: Many words searched at once; shared prefixes prune the search.
complexity: O(total characters) trie build + O(mn * 3^L) search time, L = max word length; O(total characters) space
key_idea: Build a trie of the words, storing each word at its end node. From each cell run dfs(r, c, parent): stop if the cell holds the sentinel or parent has no child for its letter; node = that child. If node holds a word, record it and clear it (avoids duplicates). Overwrite the cell with a sentinel, call dfs on each in-bounds neighbor with node, then restore the cell. Optional speedup: if node now has no word and no children, remove it from parent.

prompt: Support up to 10^5 operations on an array: point update a[i]=v and range minimum query over [l, r].
technique: Segment tree (or sqrt decomposition, O(sqrt n) per op)
signal: Range min queries mixed with point updates. Min is not invertible, so a standard Fenwick tree can't answer arbitrary [l, r] (prefixes can't be subtracted), and a sparse table can't handle updates.
complexity: O(log n) per operation, O(n) space
key_idea: Node 1 covers [0, n-1]; node covering [l, r] has children 2node ([l, m]) and 2node+1 ([m+1, r]), m = (l+r)/2; size 4n. tree[node] = min(tree[2node], tree[2node+1]), leaves hold a[i]. Update: set the leaf and recompute ancestors. Query: recurse, returning +inf when disjoint, tree[node] when fully covered, otherwise the min of both children.

prompt: For each element of an array (n up to 10^5), return how many elements to its right are smaller than it.
technique: Fenwick tree over coordinate-compressed values (merge sort also works)
signal: Count already-seen values below a threshold while scanning, with prefix sums plus updates.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
key_idea: Compress values to 1-based ranks over the sorted distinct values, so equal values share a rank. BIT of size k = number of distinct values. Scan right to left: ans[i] = query(rank[i]-1), then update(rank[i], +1). query sums bit[i] while i > 0, with i -= i&-i; update adds to bit[i] while i <= k, with i += i&-i.

prompt: Design an LRU cache with get(key) and put(key, value), both O(1), that evicts the least recently used key when over capacity.
signal: O(1) lookup combined with O(1) recency reordering.
key_idea: Map from key to node, plus a doubly linked list with sentinel head and tail; the most recent node sits right after head. get(k): if absent return -1; else unlink the node, insert it after head, return its value. put(k, v): if k exists, set its value, unlink it and insert it after head. Otherwise create a node, insert it after head, add it to the map; if the size now exceeds capacity, unlink the node before tail and delete its key from the map.

prompt: Return the first index of a non-empty needle in haystack, or -1 if it does not occur, with O(n + m) worst-case time.
signal: Exact pattern match with a linear worst-case guarantee.
key_idea: lps[i] = length of the longest proper prefix of p[:i+1] that is also its suffix. Build it with k=0, for i from 1 to m-1: while k > 0 and p[i] != p[k]: k = lps[k-1]; if p[i] == p[k]: k++; lps[i] = k. Match the same way with j=0, for each i in t: while j > 0 and t[i] != p[j]: j = lps[j-1]; if t[i] == p[j]: j++; if j == m: return i - m + 1. Return -1. The text pointer never moves backward.

prompt: Return the longest substring that occurs at least twice in s (occurrences may overlap), or "" if none exists. If several have the maximum length, return any of them. n is up to 3*10^4.
technique: Binary search on length + Rabin-Karp rolling hash (or suffix array + LCP)
signal: If a duplicate of length L exists, one of length L-1 does too (monotonic), and substrings must be compared fast.
complexity: O(n log n) average time, O(n) space
key_idea: Binary search L in [1, n-1], keeping the largest L for which check(L) finds a repeat; return that substring, or "" if none. check(L): P = B^L mod M, h = 0. For each i: h = (h*B - (s[i-L]*P if i >= L else 0) + s[i]) mod M, normalized to non-negative (add M if negative). Once i >= L-1, look up h in a map of hash -> start indices; compare the substrings on a hit to rule out collisions (or use a double hash), returning the repeat if equal; otherwise add i-L+1.

prompt: Given s consisting of lowercase letters, add characters only in front of it to make the shortest possible palindrome, and return that palindrome.
technique: Z-function or KMP prefix function on s + '#' + reverse(s)
signal: You need the longest palindromic prefix of s in linear time.
key_idea: t = s + '#' + rev(s); '#' never occurs in s, so no match crosses it. Build the KMP lps array of t; k = lps[len(t)-1] is the length of the longest palindromic prefix of s. (Z alternative: k = the largest len(t)-j over j > len(s) with j + z[j] == len(t), or 0.) Return rev(s[k:]) + s.

prompt: Return the longest palindromic substring of s in O(n) time.
technique: Manacher's algorithm (expanding around centers is O(n^2))
signal: A palindrome query with a strictly linear-time requirement.
key_idea: Transform s to T = ^#a#b#$ (the distinct sentinels stop expansion). C = R = 0. For i from 1 to len(T)-2: p[i] = min(R-i, p[2C-i]) if i < R, else 0; while T[i+1+p[i]] == T[i-1-p[i]]: p[i]++; if i+p[i] > R: C = i, R = i+p[i]. Take the i with the largest p[i]; the answer is s[(i-p[i])/2 : (i-p[i])/2 + p[i]].

prompt: In an array, every element appears exactly twice except two elements that appear once. Find those two in O(n) time and O(1) space.
technique: XOR + split by the lowest set bit
signal: Pairs cancel under XOR, and you need constant space.
key_idea: x = XOR of everything = a^b. bit = x & -x. XOR the numbers that have that bit set to get a; b = x ^ a.

prompt: For every i from 0 to n, return the number of 1 bits in i, in O(n) total.
technique: Bit recurrence (i & (i-1) drops the lowest set bit)
signal: Each value's popcount can be built from a smaller value's.
key_idea: bits[i] = bits[i & (i-1)] + 1, or bits[i] = bits[i>>1] + (i&1).

prompt: A string x divides s if s is x repeated some number of times. Given str1 and str2, return the longest string that divides both.
signal: A common repeating unit, the string analog of a common divisor.
key_idea: If s1+s2 != s2+s1, return "". Otherwise return s1[:gcd(len(s1), len(s2))]. gcd(a,b) = a if b==0 else gcd(b, a%b).

prompt: Count the primes strictly less than n, where n is up to 5*10^6.
signal: Primality for every number in a range.
complexity: O(n log log n) time, O(n) space
key_idea: If n < 2, return 0. Otherwise is[0..n-1]=true and is[0]=is[1]=false. For i from 2 while i*i < n: if is[i], mark j = i*i, i*i+i, ... < n as false. Count the true values.

prompt: Implement pow(x, n), where n is a 32-bit integer and may be negative.
signal: A large exponent rules out O(n) multiplication.
key_idea: If n<0: x=1/x and n=-n (use int64). res=1; while n: if n&1: res*=x; x*=x; n>>=1.

prompt: Compute a^b mod 1337, where b is an extremely large positive integer given as an array of its decimal digits.
technique: Modular exponentiation processing the exponent digit by digit
signal: The result needs a modulus and the exponent is too large for any numeric type.
key_idea: a = a mod 1337 first. a^(10q+d) = (a^q)^10 * a^d, so res=1; for each digit d from most significant: res = powmod(res, 10) * powmod(a, d) mod 1337. powmod is fast exponentiation, reducing mod 1337 after every multiplication.

prompt: Given the head of a linked list of unknown length, return a random node's value so that every node is equally likely, using O(1) extra space.
signal: Uniform choice from a stream of unknown length in a single pass.
key_idea: Walk the list once. For the i-th node (1-based), replace the chosen value with probability 1/i: if rand(i)==0 (rand(i) uniform in [0, i)), pick = node.val. Return pick.
